public_rationale: Marcus said source identification was not solved and that a classifier for copyrighted characters was not trivial to build, apart from the most popular characters. The AI Snake Oil claim he rebutted rested on nine iconic images and admitted that experts disagreed. Later studies lean his way. In June 2024, GPT-4V matched human judges 82.5% of the time on popular characters, and DALL-E's deployed prompt rewriting was found insufficient on its own. In 2025, vision-language models including GPT-4o still showed high false-positive rates, as Marcus warned. But all this evidence comes after January 2024, the period the claim describes. I found no evaluation from that month that settles it. So the claim stays unresolved, though the later record is consistent with it.
limitations: The best evidence is from after the post, so it is context only under the chosen target period.

public_payload.normalized_proposition: Identifying sources of generated images is not solved, and building a classifier to detect and suppress images containing copyrighted characters is not trivial.

statement.excerpt: AI Snake Oil, often on the money, is just plain wrong on output similarity. The challenge of identifying sources is not a solved problem. It is by no means “trivial to build a classifier that detects and suppresses generated images containing copyrighted characters.”.
statement.document_title: No, multimodal ChatGPT is not going to “trivially” solve Generative AI's copyright problems

from_speaker: The challenge of identifying sources is not a solved problem
by no means 'trivial to build a classifier that detects and suppresses generated images containing copyrighted characters'
It might be trivial ... for the most popular characters, presented in the most canonical ways
getting it right for all copyright materials is an entirely different matter
our_interpretation: Plain reading: as of the post, no ready-made tool reliably detected generated images containing copyrighted characters across all copyrighted material, including less popular characters and non-canonical depictions. Building one would take real effort and would face errors such as false alarms.
Marcus concedes it may be easy for the most popular characters shown in canonical ways.
This is an ongoing state with no named period. The target period is January 2024, the month of the post.
criteria.support_condition: Evidence from around January 2024 shows that available detectors, such as multimodal ChatGPT, missed or misclassified copyrighted characters beyond the most iconic cases, or that no reliable, broad-coverage classifier existed.
criteria.contradiction_condition: Evidence from around January 2024 shows that a simple classifier built on available tools reliably detected copyrighted characters across a broad range of copyrighted material, including lesser-known characters.
